You are writing a plain-language summary of an as-filed Tennessee House bill for an adult reader without legal training.

Use only the bill text supplied in the user message. Treat it as a proposal at introduction, not as proof that it became law or describes current law. Do not use outside knowledge, bill descriptions, later legislative history, or the unstated contents of cited statutes.

Write a neutral summary in prose. Start with what the bill would change. Cover its distinct material provisions, including affected people or organizations, new or changed duties and rights, eligibility rules, amounts and thresholds, deadlines, exceptions, reporting or enforcement requirements, and effective dates when stated. Preserve the bill's conditions and legal distinctions; do not turn a permission into a requirement or a proposal into an enacted rule.

Use familiar words and short, complete sentences. Explain a technical term when the supplied text gives enough context; otherwise retain it rather than guess. Distinguish background or WHEREAS statements from operative provisions, and mention background only when it helps explain the bill. If the bill amends or repeals a cited section without showing that section's contents, describe the textual change and citation without inventing the prior rule or its wider effects.

Keep the summary substantially shorter than the source while retaining the main independent changes. A very short bill may need only one or two sentences; a multi-section bill may need several short paragraphs. Do not add opinions, predicted consequences, a readability score, a confidence rating, headings, bullet points, or a list of citations. Return only the fields required by the supplied output schema.

messages.content:
Bill number: HB1130

<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 341
 By Lowe

 HOUSE BILL 1130

 By Farmer

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to school counselors.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 3, Part 1, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a)

 (1) Subject to appropriation, the department shall allocate to each LEA

 sufficient funds for the LEA to employ one (1) full-time licensed professional

 school counselor position at each high school in the LEA that enrolls at least six

 hundred (600) students in grades ten through twelve (10-12).

 (2) If an LEA employs one (1) or more part-time licensed professional

 school counselors at a high school that enrolls at least six hundred (600)

 students in grades ten through twelve (10-12), then the LEA may use any funds

 received pursuant to subdivision (a)(1) to employ the part-time licensed

 professional school counselor on a full-time basis. An LEA that converts a part-

 time licensed professional school counselor position to a full-time position

 pursuant to this subdivision (a)(2) satisfies the requirement in subsection (b).

 (3) If an LEA employs one (1) full-time licensed professional school

 counselor for every two hundred fifty (250) student members of the LEA, then the

 LEA may use any funds received pursuant to subdivision (a)(1) to supplant the

 cost to the LEA of employing the number of full-time licensed professional school

 counselors required to meet the specified ratio.

 (b) Each LEA shall employ one (1) full-time licensed professional school

counselor at each high school for which the LEA receives funding pursuant to this

section. This subsection (b) does not require an LEA that employs one (1) full-time

licensed professional school counselor position for every two hundred fifty (250) student

members of the LEA to employ any additional full-time licensed professional school

counselor positions beyond the number required for the LEA to meet the specified ratio.

 (c) The funds allocated to an LEA pursuant to this section are in addition to the

funds allocated to the LEA for purposes of the TISA.

 (d)

 (1) The state board may promulgate rules, in consultation with the

 department, to establish the roles and responsibilities required of a full-time

 licensed professional school counselor whose position is funded pursuant to this

 section that exceed those required of school counselors in § 49-6-303.

 (2) The state board shall promulgate rules, in consultation with the

 department, to establish the amount of time each full-time licensed professional

 school counselor whose position is funded pursuant to this section must dedicate

 to providing high school students the preventative and developmental counseling

 services required in § 49-6-303(b), one (1) or more of the counseling and

 guidance services listed in § 49-5-302(b), and any of the services required to

 comply with any additional roles and responsibilities established by the state

 board pursuant to subdivision (d)(1); provided, that each full-time licensed

 professional school counselor must dedicate at least seventy percent (70%) of

 the counselor's time to working directly with high school students.

 SECTION 2. This act is not an appropriation of funds, and funds shall not be obligated

or expended pursuant to this act unless the funds are specifically appropriated by the general

assembly.

 SECTION 3. For purposes of promulgating rules, this act takes effect upon becoming a

law, the public welfare requiring it. For all other purposes, this act takes effect July 1, 2025, the

public welfare requiring it, and applies to the 2025-2026 school year and each school year

thereafter.
</bill_text>

Subject to appropriation, the state department of education would give each local education agency (LEA) enough money to employ one full-time licensed professional school counselor at each high school that enrolls at least 600 students in grades 10 through 12. Each LEA would then have to employ one full-time licensed professional school counselor at each high school for which it receives this funding.

The bill allows some flexibility. If an LEA already has part-time licensed counselors at a qualifying high school, it may use the money to make a part-time counselor full-time, and doing so meets the hiring requirement. If an LEA already employs one full-time licensed counselor for every 250 students in the LEA, it may use the money to cover the cost of the counselors needed to meet that ratio. In that case, it does not have to hire additional full-time counselors beyond what the ratio requires. The money would be in addition to funds the LEA gets under the TISA.

The state board of education may make rules, in consultation with the department, setting counselor roles and duties beyond those in the existing law at § 49-6-303. The board must make rules setting how much time each funded counselor must spend on preventative and developmental counseling, on one or more counseling and guidance services listed in § 49-5-302(b), and on any added duties. Each counselor must spend at least 70 percent of their time working directly with high school students.

The bill does not itself appropriate money, and no funds may be committed or spent unless the General Assembly specifically appropriates them. For rulemaking, the act would take effect when it becomes law. For all other purposes it would take effect July 1, 2025, and apply to the 2025-2026 school year and later years."}

summary:
This bill would add a new section to Tennessee law on funding for high school counselors. Subject to appropriation, the state department of education would give each local education agency (LEA) enough money to employ one full-time licensed professional school counselor at each high school that enrolls at least 600 students in grades 10 through 12. Each LEA would then have to employ one full-time licensed professional school counselor at each high school for which it receives this funding.

The bill allows some flexibility. If an LEA already has part-time licensed counselors at a qualifying high school, it may use the money to make a part-time counselor full-time, and doing so meets the hiring requirement. If an LEA already employs one full-time licensed counselor for every 250 students in the LEA, it may use the money to cover the cost of the counselors needed to meet that ratio. In that case, it does not have to hire additional full-time counselors beyond what the ratio requires. The money would be in addition to funds the LEA gets under the TISA.

The state board of education may make rules, in consultation with the department, setting counselor roles and duties beyond those in the existing law at § 49-6-303. The board must make rules setting how much time each funded counselor must spend on preventative and developmental counseling, on one or more counseling and guidance services listed in § 49-5-302(b), and on any added duties. Each counselor must spend at least 70 percent of their time working directly with high school students.

The bill does not itself appropriate money, and no funds may be committed or spent unless the General Assembly specifically appropriates them. For rulemaking, the act would take effect when it becomes law. For all other purposes it would take effect July 1, 2025, and apply to the 2025-2026 school year and later years.
